title: Don't Ask: Understanding What Numeric Self-Reports Measure in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2603.18893v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Language models are often asked to rate their internal states with a number, but it is unclear how reliable this measure is. We train probes for four affective concepts (wellbeing, interest, focus and impulsivity) in eight instruction-tuned models to track these states over multi-turn conversations. We compare each probe's score with a numeric self-report of the same state, elicited at every turn. We find that rating questions displace the probed state, and that the rating is only weakly coupled with the probe score before the question but tracks the post-question probe much more strongly. Steering experiments suggest that models use the affective directions to inform ratings, but that relationship is not specific: ratings are associated with other concepts' probes as much as with their own, and change little when the question is about the user. translated_title: 别问了：理解语言模型中数值自我报告究竟测量了什么
translated_abstract: 语言模型经常被要求用一个数字来评估其内部状态，但这一度量的可靠性尚不清楚。我们在八个指令微调模型中，为四个情感概念（幸福感、兴趣、专注力和冲动性）训练探针，以在多轮对话中追踪这些状态。我们将每个探针的分数与每一轮对话中引导出的同一状态的数值自我报告进行比较。我们发现，评分问题本身会改变被探测的状态；评分与提问之前的探针分数仅呈弱耦合，但与提问之后的探针追踪得要紧密得多。操控实验表明，模型会利用情感方向来形成评分，但这种关系并不具有概念特异性：评分与其他概念的探针的关联程度与其自身概念的探针相当，而且当问题询问的是用户的状态时，评分几乎不发生变化。最后，提问前的耦合程度和概念特异性都不会随模型规模（1
tldr: 该研究发现语言模型的数值自我报告并不可靠地反映其内部状态：提问评分本身会扰动模型状态，评分仅在提问后与探针强相关，缺乏概念特异性，且不随模型规模而改善。
en_tdlr: Numeric self-reports in language models are unreliable measures of internal states: asking for a rating perturbs the state itself, ratings align mainly with post-question probes rather than pre-question ones, lack concept specificity, and do not improve with scale.
